The Campaign Film, Women's Fall-Winter 2026 
by Antonin Tron

Neither day nor night, L'heure du loup inhabits the fleeting moment in between. Captured by Kersti Jan Werdal, Antonin Tron's debut campaign for Balmain transforms this elusive hour into a cinematic short film, where shadow, silence and sensuality frame a new vision of the House. Leather aviator blazers, fil coupé dresses and draped silhouettes express a reinvigorated femininity — precise, instinctive and denuded of flashiness and excess.

description:
Balmain Creates Archival-Inspired Couture Look for Lalisa Manoban’s Appointment as “Amazing Thailand Ambassador”

On the occasion of Lalisa Manoban’s official appointment as Amazing Thailand Ambassador, Balmain unveiled a singular couture creation in Bangkok, worn by Lisa for this landmark moment.

A globally influential artist, performer, and cultural figure, Lisa has consistently championed Thai identity, creativity, and craftsmanship on the international stage. Her appointment recognizes both her exceptional global impact and her enduring commitment to representing Thailand with pride.

Inspired by an archival gown originally designed by Pierre Balmain for Her Majesty Queen Sirikit in 1960, the couture look pays tribute to the historic relationship between the Maison and the Royal House of Thailand — a dialogue that shaped decades of Thai–French cultural exchange.

Reinterpreted today using traditional Thai textiles and Balmain’s couture savoir-faire, the design bridges heritage and modern identity. Worn by a contemporary Thai icon and unveiled during the 170th anniversary of Thai–French relations, the creation reflects cultural continuity, craftsmanship, and the power of fashion as a shared language across generations.
title: Lalisa Manoban -  “Amazing Thailand Ambassador”

description:
80 years of Balmain : Dresses

Pierre Balmain defined the New French Style through cinched waists and strong shoulders. He dressed visionary women: from his courageous and stylish mother to intellectuals such as Gertrude Stein and Alice Toklas; from rule-breakers he dressed with confident elegance to queens and princesses navigating the balance between tradition and modernity.
title: 80 years of Balmain  : Dresses

description:
80 years of Balmain : The Balmain Jacket 

Since its debut in Pierre Balmain’s first collection in 1945, the tailored jacket has remained a signature piece. Inspired by the sharp structure and symbolism of the Breton sailor’s uniform, Balmain reinterpreted it with functional elegance, masculine in its authority, yet feminine in its silhouette.
title: 80 years of Balmain : The Balmain Jacket

description:
80 Years of Balmain: Paris

Pierre Balmain had a profound connection to Paris, a city that inspired much of his work. He often named his designs after the city itself or its iconic landmarks. Once these designs were brought to life, models were photographed against Paris’s most emblematic sites.
He introduced the new French style and the “Jolie Madame” silhouette, featuring sculpted shoulders, nipped waists, and six buttons, which defined his signature.
title: 80 years of Balmain : Paris

Architecture

In honor of Balmain’s 80 years, the House revisits its 8 defining codes, beginning with Architecture, the foundation of Pierre Balmain’s creative philosophy. His university studies in architecture, followed by an apprenticeship in couture, forged a distinctive approach that endured for more than five decades. Proclaiming that “dressmaking is the architecture of movement”, Balmain translated his love for form and structure into designs defined by bold lines, precise tailoring, and architectural silhouettes, anchored by what he referred to as “the geometric center of the dresses.”
title: 80 years of Balmain: Architecture

description:
Balmain unveils its Fall-Winter 2025 campaign, marking a bold new chapter in the house’s evolving identity driven by the vision of Creative Director Olivier Rousteing.

Photographed by Juergen Teller, the campaign comes to life within the iconic walls of Lapérouse. At the heart of the imagery is a tribute to the house’s heritage, blending '50s and '60s silhouettes with touches of '80s flair, reimagined through a modern lens. Protective shapes envelop the Balmain woman throughout her day, the soft touch of cashmere and mohair contrasting  with the boldness of leather and armor-like constructions.

The reimagined Anthem Bag takes center stage this season in a striking shade of deep burgundy, alongside bold boots that range from sharply structured to softly draped silhouettes. Across the collection, a fusion of artisanal craftsmanship and cutting-edge techniques shines, most notably in resin tiles meticulously assembled into 3D croco-effect dresses, capturing the journey of self-discovery for the modern Balmain woman.

Shot by Juergen Teller.
Creative Partner: Dovile Drizyte
Brand Art Directors: Ezra Petronio & Lana Petrusevych
Stylist: Marie-Amélie Sauvé

description:
On May 10th, the Metropolitan Museum of Art unveils « Superfine: Tailoring Black Style », a landmark exhibition that explores centuries of Black sartorial innovation, identity, and excellence.

As part of this historic moment, Balmain is honored to contribute six archival looks, continuing the dialogue between heritage and craftsmanship that defines the house’s ethos. An early glimpse into this celebration of legacy and identity awaits. Rooted in Parisian craftsmanship and shaped by Olivier Rousteing’s creative vision, these pieces honor the intersections of heritage, artistry, and cultural storytelling.

One of the hero pieces is a sculptural belt designed for Naomi Campbell, inspired by the vivid, expressive work of Ghanaian photographer Prince Gyasi. Crafted in the Balmain Atelier, the belt features black lacquered brass hands lifting a golden bouquet, a bold reinterpretation of masculine codes, worn by Naomi to close the Fall-Winter 2024 menswear show. It now joins the Costume Institute’s Spring 2025 exhibition as a striking emblem of power, grace, and distinction.

#SuperfineStyle
#CostumeInstitute

description:
Jenna Ortega embodies Balmain’s edgy, modern spirit in a striking custom-made look inspired by the art of tailoring tape & rulers. 
A poetical ode to couture and craftsmanship, the sleek sheath dress is crafted entirely from the metallic rulers used by patternmakers, placed vertically along the body to enhance the silhouette to create a bustier gown sculpted on her body.
title: Jenna Ortega at the Met Gala 2025: Tailored for You.

description:
Rosalia is a vision in custom Balmain by Olivier Rousteing. The singer wore a sculptural bodice, echoing the form of a Stockman mannequin - as archetypal piece of the couture atelier - crafted in glossy, flocked silicone, molded precisely to her own silhouette. 
Love letter to precision and uniqueness, the look is completed by a masterfully draped faille skirt wraps around the body like a meticulously handled canvas, embodying both precision and grace.
title: Rosalia at the Met Gala 2025: Tailored for You.

description:
A tribute to the timeless tradition of tailoring at the House of Balmain, Olivier Rousteing exclusively reimagined a vintage ensemble from Pierre Balmain's 1952/53 collections for her. 

Embodying Balmain’s bold and modern aesthetic, Priyanka Chopra’s look featured a structured dress with a conical bust and a delicately draped neckline, adorned with polka-dot button detailing. The jacket, with its elegant peplum, flows into a long skirt, evoking the grandeur of mid-century haute couture. A black straw hat, velvet-accented gloves, and black polka dots on an ivory background complete this sophisticated, historically rich silhouette.
title: Priyanka Chopra at the Met Gala 2025: Tailored for You.

description:
Rosalia, Priyanka Chopra, Jenna Ortega, Jeremy O. Harris and Patrick Schwarzenegger attended the 2025 Met Gala wearing custom Balmain creations by Olivier Rousteing.
This year’s dress code, « Tailored for You », paid homage to the Met’s exhibition theme « Superfine: Tailoring Black Style », with a focus on the art, heritage, and evolution of menswear.
title: The Met Gala 2025: Tailored for You.

As is the case for most Balmain collections, the Fall runway collection highlights Creative Director Olivier Rousteing's clever use of golden accents to elevate his chic Parisian tailoring. This season, those accents come to life with droll references to his childhood home.

The Balmain Homme boldly defies conventions and steers away from quiet luxury, and the Fall 2024 collection stands as a powerful statement of this rebellion.

description:
"A rose is a rose is a rose"

Last night, Olivier Rousteing presented his Balmain Spring-Summer 2024 womenswear runway at the Palais de Chaillot in Paris, in view of the ultimate Parisian symbol: the Eiffel Tower. Channeling that "New French Style" of house founder Pierre Balmain, the Creative Director pulled in the soft curves from the archives of the 1940s and early 1950s with his atelier’s architectural mastery of sculptural shapes and precision tailoring to present a collection focused on the spirit of the rose — the joy, love, and beauty associated with the flower. 

"I’d like to try to avoid the easy assumption that a florals-for-spring offering that celebrates love, beauty and joy must, by definition, be superficial. Love is complex—every rose, after all, comes with its thorns. And we wholeheartedly embrace that complexity, with thorns showing up in multiple sizes and forms throughout this runway." - Olivier Rousteing #BALMAINSS24

BALMAIN X PUMA
For the second collaboration between the house of Balmain and PUMA, Creative Director Olivier Rousteing melded Parisian luxury heritage and American basketball excitement into an exclusive capsule collection to be worn on and off the court.

#BALMAINxPUMA takes the infamous Balmain B-Court sneaker to a whole new level, reinterpreting its iconic design with an avant-garde feel and the latest groundbreaking performance materials -such as high-rebound ProFoam and high-abrasion rubber. More than a fashion statement, the #BalmainxPUMA sneaker becomes the first ever playable luxury basketball shoe, winning both in the style and sport categories.

Balmain’s distinctive Parisian savoir-faire also leads the collection’s clothing designs, with familiar American silhouettes - warm-ups, uniforms, tees, caps and even a special varsity jacket- reimagined through Olivier Rousteing’s lens.

description:
To tell the story of the #BALMAINFW22 collection, Balmain tapped visual artist Prince Gyasi for an electric reinterpretation of Antoine de Saint-Exupéry’s “Le Petit Prince”. A natural continuation after March’s Fall-Winter 2022 runway presentation – which featured quotes and inspirations from the book at the heart of the collection. Yet Gyasi’s modern interpretation pulls us away from Saint-Exupéry’s familiar watercolors: the artist opts for vibrant recreations of the story’s familiar symbols set in his hometown of Accra, Ghana, helping us to see enduring truths about acceptance, strength, and discovery with fresh eyes.

"It is much more difficult to judge oneself than to judge others."

This quote from Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's "Le Petit Prince" - displayed during the #BALMAINFW22 show - resonates particularly well with Olivier Rousteing’s most recent offering and its inspirations.

Following unpleasant experiences online through a personal journey to recovery, the Creative Director wished to highlight the freeing power of hope and transparency with designs that evoke both fragility and safety. Colored by recent events, these inspirations become evermore important, launching a collective cry for #BALMAINARMY members to unite in solidarity against hate, lies, and aggression.

A special thanks to all of our partners that made this show possible: Augustinus Bader, Le Petit Prince and the official estate of Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, and MAC Cosmetics.

*Original translation: "Il est bien plus difficile de se juger soi-même que de juger autrui."

Creative Director Olivier Rousteing presented his Balmain Fall-Winter 2022 collection live in Paris, highlighting a desire to share creative vision and allow all audiences access to elusive spaces once reserved for a happy few.

Light, delicate details mix with symbols of security and strength to evoke the true essence behind the collection: a reminder of the freeing power that comes with transparency, vulnerability, and solidarity, especially in this digital age.

Pierre Balmain’s designs were key ingredients in some of the twentieth century’s most important fashion shootings. Month after month, season after season, the house’s couture creations were worn by beautiful models in incredible locations, captured by talented photographers and published by the leading magazines. SInce this episode is centered on some of the mid-century’s most iconic fashion images, you may want to click on the webpage link to view the incredible photographs that our expert guests are describing. One of this podcast’s fashion authorities is Susanna Brown, who joins us for a second time. Brown, a photography curator and art historian, has overseen some of the most impressive photography exhibitions in recent years, including a 2012 exhibit on Cecil Beaton, a 2014 exhibit on Horst and the acclaimed 2019 show on Tim Walker—all first shown at London’s Victoria And Albert (V&A) Museum. In Episode Six , Susanna Brown spoke with us about the photographer Horst and she returns today to talk about other celebrated fashion photographers of the twentieth century and walks us through some of their most notable creations. Lynn Yaeger, the CFDA-award winning journalist who is known for her unique ability to mix an incredible design knowledge with often-amusing and always thought-provoking takes on class, politics, society and history also joins us on this episode.

description: A key person behind the rapid early growth of Balmain and smooth operations of the legendary flagship at 44 François Premier was Ginette Spanier. Spanier was the first person to be named as Balmain’s Directrice, (the Director of the house), and she remained in that position for almost thirty years. While her name may not be familiar to many today, she was a well-known personality during her time at Balmain—due not only to her superb management of the house’s rapid growth, but also to her amazing life story. It’s an incredible history that—just as the announcer of the popular television series “This Is Your Life” notes in the snippet we use to begin this episode—can be summed up as one of “fun, fear and fate.” Because Ginette Spanier was not only a genius at management—she was also a war hero. Spanier’s extraordinary history, told in a trio of best-selling autobiographies, is composed of a series of startling changes and her perfect adaptation to each of them. She began life as a rich Parisian. But, after her upper-class family moved to London, her parents lost their fortune during the Great Depression. Suddenly needing to work, Spanier transformed herself into a Fortnum and Mason salesgirl, rubbing shoulders with royals, artists and aristocrats of the time. description: Beaton, Society and BalmainSeated in the front row of the first Balmain show, alongside his friends Gertrude Stein and Alice B. Toklas, was the fascinating English Renaissance man, Cecil Beaton. The author and film director Lisa Immordino-Vreeland joins this episode of l’Atelier Balmain to discuss the fascinating life and work of Beaton. Immordino Vreeland, known for her prizewinning documentaries about some of the 20th-Century’s most talented forces in art, creation and fashion, recently focused on Beaton for her third film and second book—both titled Love Cecil—and she shares insights on his life, philosophy and creations with the podcast. From the moment he saw his first Balmain designs, Cecil Beaton began forming an important connection to the house—in fact, almost immediately after that premiere show, Beaton began to promote the young Pierre Balmain to key members of London and Paris society. description:
Gertrude, Alice and Pierre

Maira Kalman, the celebrated author, illustrator and designer joins the l’Atelier Balmain podcast for episode four. Kalman who oversaw 2020’s critically praised and colorful re-edition of Gertrude Stein’s best-selling “Autobiography of Alice B Toklas,” discusses the incredible literary and artistic legacy of Gertrude Stein and Alice B Toklas. Pierre Balmain shared a deep friendship with the couple, and he was very devoted to his pair of “American Mothers”—which is why Gertrude Stein, Alice B Toklas, along with their famous white poodle, Basket, were seated front and center at Pierre Balmain’s first show. This is the second of four episodes concentrating on the fascinating moments and personalities that played a part in the incredible story of the 1945 birth of the house of Balmain. The group of four episodes, taking its name from Alice B Toklas’ famous summation of Pierre Balmain’s first collection—A New French Style—turns to some of today’s leading writers, documentary film makers, museum curators and fashion writers for unique insights on Paris post-war style and challenges, Pierre Balmain’s fresh new style, iconic images of Balmain designs and some of the legendary personalities seated in the front row of that first house presentation. At each step, we’ll also make clear how Olivier Rousteing continues to build upon the firm foundations that Pierre Balmain established, 75 years ago. Balmain Creative Director: Olivier Roustein
title: A New French Style, Part 2: Gertrude, Alice and Pierre

description:
75 years ago, Pierre Balmain presented the very first collection of his newly established eponymous house—and that brief fashion moment, which highlighted just a few dozen designs, helped to introduce a new, golden age of post-war Parisian couture, while also establishing the firm foundations that the house of Balmain continues to build upon today. Decades later, Monsieur Balmain summed up that defining initial moment as "a miracle” —and, the truth is, everything about that very first Balmain presentation does seem almost as unbelievable as the plot line of the typical Hollywood feature film. It definitely pulls together the expected, clichéd ingredients of a blockbuster—there’s the young hero facing daunting odds, an incredibly challenging environment, a colorful cast of characters—and, of course, at the very end, an astounding and inspiring final victory.

This two-part L’Atelier Balmain podcast explores in detail the house’s first collection, with Episode Three focusing on Pierre Balmain's success in overcoming the extremely difficult conditions of post-war Paris and Episode Four placing the spotlight directly on some of the many fashion and cultural icons who attended that first show, praised the collection and helped guarantee the success of one of the Paris fashion world’s biggest post-war stars—Pierre Balmain—and his eponymous house.
title: A New French Style, Part 1: The Miracle (Podcast L’Atelier Balmain Episode 3)

Inside Balmain - Behind the scenes of Balmain's Resort 2021 Shooting with Olivier Rousteing

Get ready for the Balmain FW 2020 men's show with Evan Mock. 

Watch the #BALMAINFW20 men’s show held on the 17th of January 2020 at the Grande Halle de la Vilette in Paris.

The show marks the debut of the #BALMAINEYEWEAR by #Akoni. The unisex collection relies on the savoir-faire of the world’s best craftsmen from Japan and will be available in April 2020.

Dance performance by Jean-Charles Jousni. 

“We start with one basic truth: this is a tiny and beautiful planet, belonging to all. Here, we all share the same origin, needs and desires and any borders, (both figurative and literal), only serve to wall us off and limit us. That’s why this collection celebrates, at its heart, the beauty of the earth and sky. The runway will be filled with modern-day nomads, who are navigating seas, plains and dunes, while awed by the dazzling magnificence of the galaxies above and the earth’s tones below.
As I worked on the final looks over the holidays, the clear need for all of us to focus on that natural beauty was made even more evident to me. Watching wildfires burn and hearing about glaciers continuing to melt makes it clear that we are perhaps too focused on the small issues, while ignoring the very real danger of losing the beauty that’s right there, just in front of all of us.” - Olivier Rousteing

Discover the new #BALMAINBBUZZ bags collection: https://www.balmain.com/fr/femme/sacs...
 
The name of our latest offering is more than a simple play on alliteration. It reflects the exciting and engaging spirit of today’s Balmain—a house that continues to pay homage to its heritage and rely on the singular skills of a couture atelier, while infusing every runway with Olivier Rousteing’s desire to channel the way that his generation wishes to dress today.

This new collection looks to those runway offerings for inspiration, riffing on some of the Rousteing’s most familiar signatures, including thick fringes, quilted leathers, impressive embellishment, bold animal prints and those eye-catching black-and-white graphic patterns, which may be monochromatic but are far from monotone. To make the runway-accessory link even more explicit, the house’s famed atelier has worked closely with the teams of master Italian leather craftsmen, taking care to match BBuzz’s many color options with the same exact tones that Rousteing relied upon for his latest ready-to-wear and couture designs.

The strong lines of the BBuzz collection reflect the house’s renown tailoring, which is perhaps most often celebrated in Balmain’s iconic and transformative six-button blazer. In fact, that DB blazer’s familiar golden buttons, emblazoned with the distinctive Balmain coat-of-arms, are utilized in the collection’s adjustable straps.

The can’t-be-missed “B” adorning the front of each and every BBuzz design

To make as clear as possible the dedication that Balmain and Olivier Rousteing share for supporting the essential work of (RED) and The Global Fund, Olivier Rousteing traveled to Lyon to participate in the Global Fund Replenishment conference.  In this video, Rousteing explains why he so strongly supports the efforts of The Global Fund and (RED).

To say that I was honored to be asked to participate in the Global Fund Replenishment conference would be the understatement of the year. As a Frenchman, I am extremely proud that my country and President Macron hosted this important gathering, which brought together both government and private sector donors, in order to pledge the needed financial support for the fight to end AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria. The conference’s goal of securing $14 billion over the next three years would enable the Global Fund to support programs that could save 16 million lives. 

Those totals may be impressive, but the challenge remains a daunting one. Today, in spite of all the advances we’ve made in recent years, AIDS kills more young people than any other disease worldwide. There are 400 HIV-infected babies born every day. Today, my team and I focus on why this last stop on the Fashion Week circuit remains so distinct from the others. It’s not the runway’s styling, music and celebs that make Paris fashion so incredibly inspiring—I believe that it’s our incomparable heritage of couture and its high standards of tailoring, intricate sculpting and embellishment that distinguish us. Of course, those unique ingredients are key elements of this house’s DNA and today’s collection makes
clear what a combination of savoir-faire and a Parisian atelier can make possible.

Just as we pay homage to the singular origins of Parisian fashion, we’ve also riffed on the origins of modern-day Paris—and, actually, modern civilization itself. "Like every French kid growing up in the nineties, I was obsessed with The Fifth Element. So, obviously, there’s no need to tell me that Milla Jovovich is an incredible actor and a stunningly
beautiful woman. I’ve long admired her strength, style and talents and I’ve often dreamed of finding a way to work with Milla on a Balmain project. That’s why I was beyond excited when she agreed to sign on for our Fall-Winter campaign. I couldn’t wait to see the first images from the London shoot. I knew enough to expect great things—but, honestly, I wasn’t expecting to be so blown away, so quickly. From the moment I saw the raw footage, I knew that we had already captured exactly what we needed.

As Leeloo says in The Fifth Element, “boooooooom ba da booom.” Done. We had it. No need for complicated edits or even a soundtrack. I knew, as soon as I saw it, that all we needed to do was keep it simple and retain the focus on what Milla was doing in that incredible space. The strong, minimal style may be new for Balmain, but it perfectly compliments next fall’s styles. 

An Le’s pictures captured the same stark beauty that Jake caught on the video. I’m sure there’ll be more to come, but for now, I think we’ve got it."

Olivier Rousteing

Balmain is pleased to announce the rebirth of the historic Parisian house's accessories collection. The new bag designs for men and women, as well as the new shoe offerings, will be introduced on the 21st of January, during the presentation of the men's fall-winter and women's pre-fall collections. This new generation of Balmain accessories will be available at boutiques worldwide in June 2017.

As Creative Director Olivier Rousteing and his team developed the new lines, they relied on three distinct sources of inspiration: the house's singular history and rich archives, the Balmain atelier's continuing mastery of traditional couture techniques, and the immediately recognizable style that Rousteing has imposed upon the house over the last five years. The result is a coherent, modern offering that relies on nothing but the finest materials, craftsmen and design—in short, a truly Balmain collection.

In anticipation of the January 21st presentation, Balmain has created a special introduction to the new designs. With a spirit that reflects both Rousteing's modern outlook and the paramount importance of music for today's house, the video also introduces the golden icons that are associated with each of the accessory collection's three families: the golden coin medallion of the Renaissance line, the golden thread that works its way through the Balmain Le 44 designs, and the Domaine collection's gold-topped hotel key charm, with its long leather tassels.

Today’s runway is inspired by the unique strength of those strong women that I am so lucky to know–the Balmain women. Like them, today’s runway has stripped back all nonessential armor, allowing for a clear focus on a beautiful lightness and ease. Inevitably, there’s also a bit of myself in this collection. The calmness of today’s garden-runway reflects the spirit of a new age. Almost six years on, with more than enough battles and learning curves behind us, my team and I find ourselves settling into our comfort zone. We incorporate accomplishments, lessons learned and knowledge gained—and our evolution continues apace. The sunsets are intense, the waves incredible and the beaches immense... or at least that’s how it always seems to be as I scroll through the Instagram accounts of some of the men that we cast for our runway shows. Although I may be working late into the night on yet another weekend, at least I can escape for a few minutes via these captured moments of friends, adventures, sports and joy.

Those small cubed images were the starting point for this collection. The many beach shots helped create a digital mood board of exotic playas, praias and pantai, where friends chill after a day filled with sun, surf and swim, hoping that the night never ends—but at the same time looking forward to one more beautiful sunrise.

Designs channel the athletic, masculine and confident style that unifies this diverse tribe. The cut is easy and relaxed, with ponchos, capes, bombers and long-line sweaters playing slouchy games of proportion with joggers and voluminous trousers. What’s new for Balmain is the strong injection of color—reflecting the intense shades of the sea, sky and sand, as well as the infectious optimism of this band of revelers as they await the new day.
Here’s to new days! 

Paris
Olivier Rousteing

Balmain Spring/Summer 2015 Womenswear Show
September 25th 2014, Paris
Discover more on: http://www.balmain.com

One of the most popular photos from Balmain’s last collection didn’t focus on any of my designs: it was a shot of Rihanna, seated next to me at the after-party, and she looked amazing in her transparent top.
Was I jealous? Of course not—I was inspired!

From the strong and sexy images of my childhood—famous ‘90s supermodels, “Miss Jackson, if you’re nasty,” Madonna in her “Erotica” moment—to that night’s often-re-posted photo, it’s easy to see that my generation's popular culture has been dominated by one long, uninterrupted line of beautiful, confident women, proud of their bodies and unafraid to explore sensuality and transparency.
You have to admire the way so many of these stars manage to turn the tables on censorship. They can’t be banned. We search for unbleeped videos, hashtag to free closed Instagram accounts and google photos unmarred by thick black bands. Their creations and public images celebrate today’s refreshingly honest and upbeat sexuality—and they have been a major inspiration for this collection, pushing me channel their spirit into fluid transparent layers, surprising exposures of skin and unexpected touches of clear plastic. The often bright and optimistic spirit of their pop creations can be seen in this collection’s sharp tailoring, bold colors and unusual graphic mixes.

For his first runway collection as the house's Designer, Olivier Rousteing maintains Balmain's
couture signature, with a focus on complex embellishment and bold, new proportions. Inspired by
the androgyny of bullfighters' traditional "traje de luces" and the performance jumpsuits that Nudie
Cohn designed for country and western stars during Las Vegas' golden years of the early 60s,
Rousteing gives Balmain's sharp tailoring a palette of celestial white, sky blue, graphic black and
shining silver and gold with assorted pastels.
The patterned jackets and pants mix leathers and fabrics in the arabesque patterns found on
traditional cowboy boots and Deco embroidery underscores the anatomy. Spring's high-rise waist
is cinched by belts with outsize buckles. Rousteing's take on the toreador's bolero jacket is
cropped in front with a long back. Patchwork dresses mix fine embroidery, quilting and beading in
collage style.
Balmain's softer side is evident in the pajama suits with beaded tunics, cape jackets, tunic shirts,
flowing gaucho skirts and trousers in silk or glove-like kid leather. The Balmain biker jacket has a
feminine touch, shown with beaded tees under matching vests.
